spec.description:
clock_last_meas:
The timestamp of the last measurement received from the NTP server.
Chrony Tracking Log Equivalent: This corresponds to the time of the last update (not directly shown in chronyc tracking but can be seen with chronyc sources).

clock_last_update (Collectd):
The time of the last clock update.
Chrony Tracking Log Equivalent: This indicates when the last update to the system clock occurred, matching the Date and Time fields in the tracking log.
spec.title: Chrony - Clock Last Measure

spec.description:
frequency_error:
Represents the frequency error in parts per million (ppm), showing the difference between the system clock and the reference clock.
Chrony Tracking Log Equivalent: Matches the Freq ppm (Frequency offset) field in the tracking log.
spec.title: Chrony - Frequency Error

spec.description:
time_offset:
The time offset between the system clock and the NTP server.

root_delay :
The total network delay to the NTP server, including all intermediate hops.

root_dispersion :
The total dispersion or uncertainty of the time from the reference clock.
spec.title: Chrony - Time Offset

spec.description:
Skew ppm (Skew in parts per million)
The estimated error (or "skew") in the frequency offset measurement, in parts per million.
A lower value means the frequency offset is well-known and stable.
Example: 0.100 ppm, meaning the error in the frequency measurement is quite small.
spec.title: Chrony - Skew PPM

Root Mean Square (RMS) offset:
The RMS offset indicates how much the system clock typically deviates from the reference time (i.e., the time provided by the NTP server).
A lower RMS offset means the clock is more accurately synchronized with the reference time.

spec.description:
slab_recl
This parameter represents the number of objects that are currently in a "reclaimed" state within the slab allocator.
Reclaimed objects are those that have been freed but are still retained by the slab cache for potential reuse. This helps reduce the overhead of repeated allocations and deallocations, allowing for faster access to memory.
Monitoring slab_recl can help you understand how efficiently memory is being reused and whether there is sufficient slab cache available for the application’s needs.

--

Slab Allocator:
The slab allocator is a memory management mechanism in the Linux kernel that manages memory in chunks (called "slabs") for objects of the same size. It is particularly efficient for managing memory for objects that are frequently allocated and deallocated, such as kernel data structures.
spec.title: Memory - Slab reclaimed

spec.description:
slab_unrecl:
This parameter indicates the number of objects that are currently in an "unreclaimed" state.
Unreclaimed objects are those that are currently allocated and in use, meaning they cannot be reused until they are freed. This can indicate how much memory is actively being utilized by the system or application.
Monitoring slab_unrecl is important for understanding memory pressure and can help identify potential memory shortages if the number of unreclaimed objects is consistently high.
